Alright, listen up, kid. You're here to learn about levels in a live music setting, so pay attention.

First off, always check your equipment before the performance starts. Make sure the soundboard, monitors, and microphones are all functioning properly.

Next, balance the levels for each instrument. Start with the drums, set the kick and snare at around -10 dB, and the rest of the drums at -5 dB. For guitars, bass, and vocals, adjust each one individually based on their volume in the mix. Aim for vocals around -3 dB, guitars around 0 dB, and bass around -5 dB.

Don't forget about the audience. The main speakers should be set slightly louder than the monitors to ensure everyone in the venue can hear clearly.

Lastly, during the performance, keep an ear out for any feedback issues and quickly adjust levels as needed. Good luck! Now, get back to work.
